\section{Hamiltonian-response exhaustion}

The predicate is narrow because the target is narrow. A broader predicate would not refute the theorem; it would define a different theorem object by admitting additional anchors, operator load, open/update ledgers, nonlocal structure, boundary data, or richer projection content.

Before the exhaustion proof begins, fix the comparator boundary. This argument is not canonical quantization, not path integration, and not a Galilei-covariance derivation repackaged. Those comparators operate after a quantum carrier and kinematic assumptions have already been admitted. The AASC proof first licenses the projective-Hilbert projection from AMetric non-selection, fixes state/phase/norm/operator roles, declares the minimal nonrelativistic spatial envelope, defines the same-scope first-response predicate, and then exhausts the operator candidates.

\begin{definition}[General local second-order scalar candidate]
Inside the declared scalar envelope $\Hilb=L^2(Q,dx)$, a local linear differential candidate of order at most two has schematic form
\[
H=A^{ij}(x)\partial_i\partial_j+B^i(x)\partial_i+C(x),
\]
or, after domain-sensitive integration by parts, an equivalent divergence-form presentation. The coefficients are not automatically admissible. Each coefficient family must be typed as admitted metric/scalar structure, declared tensor/operator load, skin, or hidden selector.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Linearity and representative operator status]
A same-scope closed Hamiltonian generator must be linear on the representative Hilbert carrier. Nonlinear dependence on $\psi$ adds state-dependent tensor/source load, composition-context dependence, or effective/open scope.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The standing-bearing state is a ray, and representative choices are skin modulo the projective quotient. A nonlinear generator depending on a chosen representative, decomposition, normalization convention, density, expectation value, or composite context assigns different continuation behavior to the same projective content unless additional state-dependent load is declared. Under independent composition, such dependence becomes a hidden carrier or source ledger. The closed same-scope branch therefore admits linear representative generators. Nonlinear equations may be physically meaningful as mean-field, effective, stochastic, or open-system dynamics; then they are no longer undeclared same-scope closed generators.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Self-adjointness and domain standing]
A closed same-scope Hamiltonian generator must be self-adjoint on its declared domain, or essentially self-adjoint with a declared closure. Otherwise norm/probability standing fails or the system is open/effective.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $i\hbar\partial_t\psi=H\psi$,
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\langle\psi,\psi\rangle
=\frac{i}{\hbar}\langle H\psi,\psi\rangle-\frac{i}{\hbar}\langle\psi,H\psi\rangle .
\]
The expression vanishes on a common domain when $H$ is symmetric there, but closed reversible continuation requires a self-adjoint generator, not merely a formal symmetric expression. If a symmetric operator has multiple self-adjoint extensions, the extension choice is domain/boundary data and must be declared. A hidden extension choice is selector import. Non-self-adjoint generators may represent effective loss/gain, absorbing boundaries, or open dynamics, but not closed same-scope continuation \cite{MaleySelfAdjoint,ReedSimon}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Principal-symbol scalarity]
If the second-order principal symbol carries no declared tensor load beyond the flat spatial metric $\delta^{ij}$, then
\[
A^{ij}(x)=a\,\delta^{ij}
\]
with constant $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The coefficient $A^{ij}(x)$ is a symmetric contravariant tensor field or principal-symbol datum. If it is not proportional to $\delta^{ij}$, it selects anisotropic directions and therefore imports tensor load. If it varies over $Q$, it supplies a medium, curved configuration metric, variable mass profile, or background scalar/tensor field. If such data are declared, the theory has moved to enriched scope. If they are not declared, they are hidden selectors. The minimal same-scope scalar envelope contains only the flat metric and constant projection coefficient, so the principal symbol is $a\delta^{ij}$ and the second-order slot is $a\Delta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[First-order term classification]
A first-order term
\[
B^i(x)\partial_i
\]
is not an undeclared same-scope scalar first-response Hamiltonian term.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The coefficient $B^i$ is a vector field or connection-like object. If it is standing-bearing, it imports a preferred direction, drift field, gauge connection, moving frame, or boundary/domain datum. If it is pure gauge, the gauge structure must be declared. If it is not paired with the required lower-order correction, it fails symmetry and hence closed standing. If it arises from boundary behavior, the boundary condition is an anchor. Therefore no bare first-derivative term survives inside the minimal scalar envelope. Declared electromagnetic coupling, drift, or connection terms are legitimate enriched-scope structures, not hidden minimal alternatives.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Affine momentum and boost ledger classification]
A constant first-order self-adjoint term such as
\[
v\cdot p=-i\hbar v^i\partial_i
\]
does not refute the normal form. When paired with the quadratic kinetic branch,
\[
\frac{p^2}{2m}+v\cdot p+C
=\frac{(p+mv)^2}{2m}+C-\frac{m|v|^2}{2}.
\]
It is therefore one of: inertial-frame or Galilean-boost anchor motion; a momentum-origin convention with homogeneous energy-baseline shift; a declared drift/effective ledger; or, if undeclared, a hidden preferred-frame selector. It is not an additional minimal scalar first-response slot.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The vector $v$ is not supplied by the minimal scalar spatial envelope. If it records a boost or moving frame, the carrier presentation has changed by an inertial-frame ledger; completing the square returns the same quadratic kinetic form plus a baseline energy shift. If $v$ records physical drift, current, or environment motion, it is declared tensor/operator load. If no such declaration is made, the vector selects a preferred direction and momentum origin. Hence the affine momentum term is classified rather than admitted as a new same-scope slot.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Zeroth-order scalar slot]
The only same-scope local scalar multiplicative operator with no spatial derivative is
\[
V(x),
\]
where $V$ is a declared real scalar potential/source ledger on a domain for which the total Hamiltonian is self-adjoint or has a declared self-adjointness certificate.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A zeroth-order local operator multiplies the scalar wavefunction by a scalar function. If the multiplier is constant, it contributes a homogeneous energy/phase baseline. If it varies over the admitted spatial carrier, it is scalar potential content. Matrix-valued, stochastic, nonlocal, gauge-coupled, history-dependent, or state-dependent multipliers add structure beyond the minimal scalar envelope.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Higher-response and nonlocal exclusion]
Higher derivatives, fractional Laplacians, inverse operators, integral kernels, memory terms, pseudodifferential symbols, and arbitrary functions of $\Delta$ are higher-response, effective, or nonlocal continuation-envelope expansions rather than minimal same-scope first-response Hamiltonian content.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The predicate admits the first nontrivial scalar spatial response. Operators such as $\Delta^2$, $f(\Delta)$, $(-\Delta)^\alpha$, inverse operators, integral kernels, time-memory maps, and pseudodifferential symbols require higher spatial response, arbitrary operator-function selection, nonlocal continuation, or effective expansion. These may be legitimate when declared, but they are not undeclared first-response content.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Gauge, spin, relativistic, topological, and boundary exclusions]
Gauge connection, spin coupling, relativistic structure, topology-sensitive connection data, and boundary/domain selection are legitimate when declared, but they are not undeclared same-scope minimal first-response Hamiltonian content.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Gauge coupling replaces $\partial_i$ by a covariant derivative and imports connection content. Spin coupling introduces internal matrix/operator content. Relativistic wave equations change the spacetime projection, representation class, or time-derivative order. Aharonov--Bohm-type terms import topology/gauge data. Boundary conditions or self-adjoint extension choices are external operator data unless fixed by the declared domain. Each case is richer, effective, declared, or boundary-enriched scope rather than an undeclared same-scope alternative.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Hamiltonian-response normal form]
If $\SameScopeQ(H)$ in the minimal nonrelativistic scalar spatial envelope, then
\[
H=a\Delta+M_V,
\]
where $a$ is a constant projection-envelope coefficient and $M_V$ is the multiplication operator associated with the declared scalar potential/source ledger. The dimensional interpretation of $a$ requires action/inertial scale anchoring.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By linearity and domain discipline, $H$ is a representative linear operator on a declared dense Hilbert domain. By closed continuation, it is self-adjoint or essentially self-adjoint with declared closure. Locality and first-response order reduce the candidate to the general second-order local form
\[
A^{ij}(x)\partial_i\partial_j+B^i(x)\partial_i+C(x).
\]
Principal-symbol scalarity gives $A^{ij}=a\delta^{ij}$ with constant $a$, hence the second-order contribution $a\Delta$. The first-order classification and affine-momentum lemmas exclude $B^i\partial_i$ unless vector, gauge, drift, boost/frame, or domain load is declared, in which case the term is retyped as anchor motion, baseline convention, or enriched/effective scope. The zeroth-order lemma leaves $C=V$ as scalar potential/source ledger. Higher derivative, nonlocal, gauge, spin, relativistic, nonlinear, open, measurement, and boundary-selection alternatives are excluded by the predicate or retyped as declared richer/effective/open/update/boundary scope. Hence every surviving minimal same-scope candidate has normal form $H=a\Delta+M_V$.
\end{proof}

\section{Unitary compatibility and generator form}

\begin{theorem}[Closed continuation generator theorem]
If $U_t$ is a strongly continuous closed reversible standing-preserving one-parameter group on the representative Hilbert projection, then
\[
U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}
\]
for a self-adjoint $H$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Closed trajectory coherence gives transition-probability preservation at ray level. Wigner implementation and continuous-time branch selection give a unitary representative group. Stone's theorem gives a self-adjoint generator. The factor $\hbar$ records the admitted action/phase scale rather than a boundary-generated value.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Hamiltonian normal-form insertion]
For the minimal scalar nonrelativistic spatial projection,
\[
\SameScopeQ(H)\Rightarrow H=a\Delta+M_V .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
This is the Hamiltonian-response normal-form theorem from Part VI. It is repeated here to show the exact insertion point in the closed-continuation chain.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficient fixation after inertial/action scale anchoring]
The AASC-native spatial normal-form theorem gives $H=a\Delta+M_V$. The numerical coefficient is fixed only after the nonrelativistic inertial/action scale anchors are admitted. In a nonrelativistic scalar particle projection with admitted action scale $\hbar$, inertial mass anchor $m$, and free-particle dispersion
\[
E(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2m},
\]
the kinetic coefficient in $H=a\Delta$ is
\[
a=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the Fourier representation rather than treating plane waves as normalizable states. The Laplacian acts spectrally as
\[
\Delta\leftrightarrow -|k|^2,
\]
and the admitted action/phase scale gives $p=\hbar k$. Thus the kinetic branch $a\Delta$ has spectral value $-a|k|^2$. Matching the admitted nonrelativistic inertial dispersion
\[
E=\frac{|p|^2}{2m}=\frac{\hbar^2|k|^2}{2m}
\]
requires
\[
-a=\frac{\hbar^2}{2m},\qquad a=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}.
\]
This step is not AMetric numerical generation of $m$ or $\hbar$; it is coefficient fixation after the nonrelativistic inertial/action anchors are admitted.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Projective Galilei representation witness]
A stronger conventional-facing route identifies mass as the central charge in the projective representation of the Galilei group \cite{Bargmann1954}. The present theorem does not require deriving the Galilei representation from below. It uses the nonrelativistic inertial/transport anchor exactly where coefficient normalization is needed, while preserving the AASC distinction between form standing and numerical scale standing.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Degenerate homogeneous branch]
If $a=0$ in the Hamiltonian normal form, the surviving generator $H=V$ is pure local potential/phase evolution. It may represent a homogeneous baseline or local potential ledger, but it is not the general spatial kinetic response branch. The Schr\"odinger theorem therefore uses the nontrivial spatial-response branch $a\neq 0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}[Closed-source Schr\"odinger form]
For the closed same-scope nonrelativistic Hamiltonian projection,
\[
i\hbar\partial_t\psi=
\left(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta+M_V\right)\psi.
\]
\end{corollary}

\section{Schr\"odinger dynamics as the unique minimal first-response Hamiltonian projection}


\begin{theorem}[Main theorem: closed autonomous Schr\"odinger projection]
\label{thm:main-schrodinger}
Let a nondegenerate determinate admissible quantum predictive interior $\mathfrak S$ instantiate the kernel
\[
K=(\Adm,\Stand,\ARef,\Irr),
\]
the fixed-domain consequence layer $A^+$, and only the exact representative
certificate $c_{\mathfrak S}^{\rm QP}$.  Import W9.19 first to construct
\[
 (P_{\mathfrak S},q_{\mathfrak S},\bar p_{\mathfrak S},
  \bar C_{\mathfrak S},\bar\boxtimes_{\mathfrak S};
  c_{\mathfrak S}^{\rm QS}).
\]
Let a separately constructed faithful closed nonrelativistic
projective-Hilbert projection
\[
 \Pi_{\rm NR}:P_{\mathfrak S}\longrightarrow\mathbb P L^2(\RR^d,dx)
\]
preserve the derived standing, transition weight, continuation, and declared
independent-composition law, and use the primary full-space minimal envelope
\[
\Pi_H(A_Q)=(\RR^d,\delta,dx,\Hilb,\ProjHilb,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle,D(H)),
\qquad \Hilb=L^2(\RR^d,dx).
\]
Let closed reversible continuation preserve transition-probability standing on rays, let Wigner implementation, projective phase lifting, and strong continuity give a phase-fixed unitary group $U_t$, and let Stone's theorem supply its self-adjoint generator $H$. Let $H$ satisfy $\SameScopeQ(H)$ as a nontrivial general spatial-response candidate. Let $M_V$ be the multiplication operator associated with the declared scalar potential/source ledger and with a domain/self-adjointness certificate for the total Hamiltonian, and let $\hbar,m$ be admitted action/inertial scale anchors. Then the unique minimal first-response same-scope closed autonomous Hamiltonian evolution form is
\[
i\hbar\partial_t\psi=
\left(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta+M_V\right)\psi .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The kernel and $A^+$ fix target, standing, admissibility, reference,
irreversibility, AMetric no-selector discipline, no same-act repair, and no
hidden same-scope discriminator.  Theorem~\ref{thm:w919-import} is applied to
$c_{\mathfrak S}^{\rm QP}$ and supplies the standing-bearing quotient,
separated $\bar p_{\mathfrak S}$, descended $\bar C_{\mathfrak S}$ and
$\bar\boxtimes_{\mathfrak S}$, and their naturality.  None is reconstructed
later from Hilbert or Hamiltonian data.  Those conclusions type the domain and
preservation obligations of $\Pi_{\rm NR}$; without W9.19 the displayed
projection is not a map from a certified standing object.  Faithful
projective-Hilbert projection then licenses
$(\RR^d,\delta,dx,\Hilb,\ProjHilb,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle,D(H))$ as
representative geometry and primary full-space spatial envelope, not primitive
foundation. Boundary-trace fixation fixes state, phase, norm/probability,
operator-domain, potential/source, and measurement/update roles as role-anchor
equivalence classes without representative selection. Coherent projected
quantum trajectory dynamics gives closed norm/probability and
transition-probability continuation. Wigner implementation gives unitary or
antiunitary representatives; strong continuous one-parameter time
continuation selects the unitary branch, and the projective phase-lift lemma
fixes a representative unitary group up to homogeneous energy-baseline
ledger. Stone's theorem then gives a self-adjoint generator $H$ and abstract
Schr\"odinger form. The predicate $\SameScopeQ(H)$ applies to the spatial
Hamiltonian side inside the declared minimal spatial envelope. By
Hamiltonian-response exhaustion,
\[
H=a\Delta+M_V.
\]
The potential ledger includes the domain/self-adjointness certificate required for closed unitary continuation. Nonrelativistic inertial/action scale anchoring fixes
\[
a=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}.
\]
Therefore
\[
i\hbar\partial_t\psi=
\left(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta+M_V\right)\psi.
\]
Any alternative inside the target is skin, anchor motion, hidden operator load, richer scope, effective/open/update scope, boundary-domain enrichment, or standing failure.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope of uniqueness]
Uniqueness is uniqueness of form within the declared closed autonomous scalar nonrelativistic projective-Hilbert projection envelope and up to declared scale anchors $\hbar,m$, potential multiplication ledger $M_V$, and domain conditions. It is not uniqueness of all quantum dynamics and not exclusion of declared richer-scope theories.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Declared-domain extension]
For a declared regular spatial domain $Q\subseteq\RR^d$, the same local Hamiltonian form holds only relative to an explicit domain, boundary, and self-adjointness certificate. Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, periodic, Friedrichs, deficiency-index, and other extension selections are anchors of the declared domain problem, not hidden same-scope alternatives to the primary full-space theorem.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Changing from $\RR^d$ to $Q\subseteq\RR^d$ introduces boundary and extension data. If those data are declared and the total Hamiltonian has a self-adjoint realization, the local scalar first-response form remains $a\Delta+M_V$ on that domain. If they are not declared, the candidate imports a hidden selector and fails same-scope standing.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Paired-projection architecture as a unification foothold]
Together with the corresponding Einstein metric-projection theorem \cite{MaleyEinsteinDynamics}, the result yields the paired projection schema
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\text{AASC standing-preserving continuation}\\
&\Rightarrow
\begin{cases}
\text{faithful metric projection}\Rightarrow\text{Einstein dynamics},\\
\text{faithful projective-Hilbert projection}\Rightarrow\text{Schr\"odinger dynamics}.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\]
This is not yet a full quantum-gravity theory. It is the common normal-form basis for a later unification theorem: the two flagship dynamics are distinct faithful projections of one upstream admissibility/standing/continuation kernel.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Not yet a joint dynamics theorem]
The paired projection schema is deliberately not reported as a full quantum-gravity theory or joint metric/projective-Hilbert dynamics. It is a unification foothold: the two flagship dynamics are no longer independent primitives but distinct faithful projections of the same upstream admissibility/standing/continuation discipline. A later theorem must supply the joint compatibility carrier.
\end{remark}
